preamble: The voiced velar plosive /g/ became a voiceless uvular fricative [χ] in northern Dutch and in Afrikaans. West Germanic geminate *gg, which was a true stop, fricativized in Dutch; the resulting fricative merged with /x/ in the north as a post-velar or uvular [χ] (the 'harde g'), and Afrikaans /χ/ spelled g is most often uvular. Single Proto-Germanic *g was already a fricative in this area, so only the geminate cases continue a genuine stop. The change is confined to Low Franconian.

examples.note: In the north /ɣ/ and /x/ are realized the same, described as a voiceless post-velar [x̠] or uvular [χ] fricative.
Afrikaans /χ/, spelled g, is most often uvular, a fricative [χ] or voiceless trill [ʀ̥]; compare goed /χut/ 'good'.

sources: Gussenhoven, C. (1992). Dutch. Journal of the International Phonetic Association, 22(2), 45–47. https://doi.org/10.1017/S002510030000459X
